$comment: Which documents may name a contract number, and what naming one obliges them to. See scripts/check-documentation-authorities.mjs for the rules and docs/ops/documentation-authorities.md for why this exists.

authorities.why: Agent operating rules state the repository and hosted contracts directly.
Session summary; states the current implementation boundary.
Detailed inventory; its delivered/outstanding marks move with each contract.
Execution sequence; its next-step list is falsified by the contract that does the step.
The declared live implementation and hosted-status authority.
Feature and safeguard classification; its backend overlay moves with the backend.
ADR index; each row carries an implementation status.
Design index; carries the merged-delta table against the plan's snapshot.
Carries a dated progress overlay above a frozen planning record.

Risk dispositions name the contract that resolved them. Its contract references are per-item dispositions naming what resolved an entry, not a claim about current state, so it is required only never to name a contract that does not exist yet.

Decision dispositions name the contract that implemented them. Its contract references are per-item dispositions naming what resolved an entry, not a claim about current state, so it is required only never to name a contract that does not exist yet.

An inventory of what the schema currently binds. It is held in step by tests/database-parity/stageCTriggerBindingCoverage.test.ts against a real database, which is a stronger check than counting contract numbers in prose.
